input-and-type-conversion.label: Input and Type Conversion
input-and-type-conversion.summary: Read user input as text, convert numeric text with `int()` or `float()`, and use `str()` when a number must become part of a text message.

sketch_input_returns_text.title: input() always gives you text
sketch_input_returns_text.bodyMarkdown:
`input()` pauses the program and reads what the user types. The value it returns is always a string.

```python
name = input()
print(name)
```

If the user types:

```text
Maya
```

then `name` stores the string `"Maya"`.

The same rule applies when the characters look numeric. If the user types `42`, `input()` still returns the string `"42"`.

That distinction matters because text and numbers behave differently. Reading input is the first step; converting it is a separate step when your program needs numeric behavior.

sketch_convert_numbers.title: Convert numeric input before doing math
sketch_convert_numbers.bodyMarkdown:
Because `input()` returns text, numeric input must be converted before you use it as a number.

Use `int()` for whole numbers:

```python
age_text = input()
age = int(age_text)
print(age + 1)
```

If the user types `12`:

- `age_text` is the string `"12"`;
- `int(age_text)` produces the integer `12`;
- `age + 1` produces `13`.

You can also convert directly:

```python
age = int(input())
```

Use `float()` when decimal values are allowed:

```python
price = float(input())
print(price * 2)
```

If the user types `3.5`, `price` becomes the number `3.5`.

sketch_str_and_output.title: Convert a number to text when building a message
sketch_str_and_output.bodyMarkdown:
Sometimes your program has a number but needs to place that number inside a larger string.

```python
count = 7
message = "You have " + str(count) + " points"
print(message)
```

`str(count)` converts the integer `7` into the string `"7"`, so all three pieces can be joined as text.

Without that conversion, this expression mixes incompatible values:

```python
"You have " + count
```

For this lesson, remember the direction of each conversion:

- `int("12")` → number `12`
- `float("3.5")` → number `3.5`
- `str(12)` → text `"12"`

Choose the conversion based on what the next operation needs.
